assessment.profile_description: Standard security assessment: passive set plus nmap web ports, exposed-file probes, gobuster, nikto and nuclei with safe settings.

authorization.statement: Operator confirmed ownership of, or written permission to test, the in-scope assets.

findings.title: Cookie without HttpOnly attribute
findings.description: Cookies without HttpOnly can be read by JavaScript and stolen through XSS.

cvss.justification: Not scored: no directly demonstrated impact, or insufficient evidence for a defensible CVSS vector.

findings.evidence: Cookie names (values not stored): PHPSESSID PHPSESSID security
findings.impact: Session cookies may be exposed to script access or sent over insecure channels, increasing the risk of session theft.
findings.remediation: Set the HttpOnly attribute on cookies that JavaScript does not need.
findings.false_positive_notes: Cookies used only for client-side preferences may legitimately omit HttpOnly.

findings.title: Directory listing enabled
findings.description: The web server lists directory contents, exposing file names and potentially sensitive files.

cvss.justification: Directory index confirmed readable without authentication; sensitivity of the listed files was not assessed, so confidentiality impact is scored Low.

findings.evidence: GET /config/ -> HTTP 200; auto-index page detected: Index of /config
findings.impact: Technical details help attackers choose and tune attacks against the system.
findings.remediation: Disable directory indexing (Options -Indexes, autoindex off) and review exposed files.
findings.false_positive_notes: Intentional public file mirrors may be listed on purpose.

findings.title: Cookie without SameSite attribute
findings.description: Without SameSite, cookies are sent on cross-site requests in older browsers, aiding CSRF.

cvss.justification: Not scored: no directly demonstrated impact, or insufficient evidence for a defensible CVSS vector.

findings.evidence: Cookie names (values not stored): PHPSESSID PHPSESSID security
findings.impact: Session cookies may be exposed to script access or sent over insecure channels, increasing the risk of session theft.
findings.remediation: Set SameSite=Lax or Strict (None only with Secure when required).
findings.false_positive_notes: Modern browsers default to Lax, reducing the practical risk.

findings.title: Missing Content-Security-Policy header
findings.description: No CSP is set, so the browser has no policy limiting where scripts and other resources may load from, reducing defence against XSS.

cvss.justification: Not scored: no directly demonstrated impact, or insufficient evidence for a defensible CVSS vector.

findings.evidence:
HTTP/1.1 302 Found
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 06:30:28 GMT
Server: Apache/2.4.25 (Debian)
Set-Cookie: PHPSESSID=<redacted>; path=/
Expires: Thu, 19 Nov 1981 08:52:00 GMT
Cache-Control: no-store, no-cache, must-revalidate
Pragma: no-cache
Set-Cookie: PHPSESSID=<redacted>; path=/
Set-Cookie: security=<redacted>
Location: login.php
Content-Length: 0
Content-Type: text/html; charset=UTF-8
findings.impact: Browsers are not instructed to apply defence-in-depth protections, which makes exploitation of other flaws (XSS, clickjacking, downgrade attacks) easier.
findings.remediation: Define a restrictive Content-Security-Policy (avoid unsafe-inline/unsafe-eval).
findings.false_positive_notes: Severity is context dependent; static or non-sensitive sites may accept this risk.

findings.title: Version information disclosed in server header
findings.description: The server header discloses software and version details that help attackers select exploits.

cvss.justification: Not scored: no directly demonstrated impact, or insufficient evidence for a defensible CVSS vector.

findings.evidence: server: Apache/2.4.25 (Debian)
findings.impact: Technical details help attackers choose and tune attacks against the system.
findings.remediation: Remove or genericise version banners (e.g. ServerTokens Prod, server_tokens off, expose_php=Off).
findings.false_positive_notes: Disclosure alone is not exploitable; it only reduces attacker effort.

limitations: Point-in-time, unauthenticated black-box assessment; authenticated areas, session handling after login and business logic were not tested.
Automated scanners produce false positives and false negatives; every finding classified as Potential or Unverified requires manual validation.
No exploitation, credential extraction, data modification, file upload, brute-force or denial-of-service testing was performed.
Only approved hosts and ports were contacted; redirects to unapproved destinations were not followed.
Wordlist-based discovery cannot prove absence of content; JavaScript-rendered routes and authenticated API endpoints were not enumerated.
OWASP Top 10 mapping is indicative. It does not establish compliance or non-compliance with any standard.
CVSS scores are provided only where the evidence supports a defensible vector; all other findings are intentionally not scored.
Nikto manages its own TLS handling; DOXA cannot enforce certificate validation inside Nikto, Nuclei or WhatWeb.
